text:
maria: hitting a weird outage in us-east-1 — a bunch of edge proxies are returning 502/504 for model pulls and logs show connection resets. CloudWatch alert for high SNAT port utilization popped at 15:32 UTC :warning:
ajay: seen similar on prod yesterday. could be ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT gateways. how broad is the impact?
rachel: traces show <10ms DNS and successful TCP handshakes up to system calls, then lots of sockets stuck in TIME_WAIT. app logs: 
```
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
rpc: connection error: EOF
```
kim: Deploy-bot reports increased 5xx on the /model/pull endpoint across multiple zones. No config changes rolled out in the last 6 hours.
maria: Confirmed scope: most requests originate from sidecar model pullers and transient batch workers that open many short-lived HTTP sessions.
ajay: NAT gateway has finite SNAT slots per elastic IP, with many concurrent ephemeral source ports consumed. We saturated SNAT translation entries.
rachel: quick repro: spawn 10k short clients that open/close connections quickly -> port pool drains fast.
ajay: mitigation options: 1) add more NAT GW (more EIPs), 2) enable node-local SNAT (masquerade per node), 3) reduce egress by moving to VPC endpoints for S3/ECR, 4) increase connection reuse from clients.
kim: can we throttle model pullers? Add client-side backoff and reuse HTTP keepalives?
maria: yes, urgent short-term: rate-limit pulls at edge-proxy layer and enable aggressive keepalive pooling for the model fetcher. Medium-term: VPC endpoints + per-AZ NAT to spread load.
rachel: patch ready to enable connection pooling in the model fetcher (HTTP/1.1 keepalive + max sockets 100). small config that flips on within app.
ajay: ops can spin up additional NAT GWs in other AZs and add route table entries. I'll queue that but AWS has a warm-up delay.
deply-bot: cloudwatch-alert: SNATUtilization > 95% on nat-gw-az1, nat-gw-az2 (incident id: CN-19265).
kim: is it feasible to use inline proxies (per-node squid/nginx) to reduce connections to central NAT? Node-local proxies would keep TCP pools per-node and reduce SNAT churn.
ajay: yep node-local SNAT (ip-masq-agent + NAT on each node) would avoid hairpinning through central gateway for egress from pods to public. Requires careful iptables rules and testing.
maria: immediate actions: (1) enable model-fetcher keepalive patch (rachel) (2) add extra NAT gateways in us-east-1 (ajay) (3) open ticket to evaluate node-local SNAT and VPC endpoints (kim).
rachel: rolling patch to canary now — will monitor connection reuse metric and tokenized error rate.
ajay: provisioning NAT GWs now, attaching additional EIPs and updating route tables for az failover. ETA 20m.
kim: also let's add a Grafana panel for ephemeral_port_usage and TIME_WAIT count by instance. Missing metrics today slowed diagnosis.
maria: +1 on metrics. Also add a dashboard for app-level connection pool utilization.
deply-bot: deploy: model-fetcher v2.3.1 -> canary (maria@prod). status: started.
rachel: canary looks good so far, error rate down by ~60% on canary hosts. TIME_WAIT trending down.
ajay: NAT additions are active in two AZs. SNAT metrics falling to ~60%.
maria: ok keep watching for 30m before removing rate-limits. thanks all :thumbsup:
kim: follow-ups: document NAT capacity plan, set threshold alerts at 70% port usage, investigate using VPC endpoints for S3/ECR to cut 40% of pulls. I'll own the doc.
maria: assigning postmortem if we still see blips after mitigations. otherwise mark as ttr reduced incident.
ajay: any thoughts on connection reuse for our sidecars (envoy) — should we force http2 multiplexing?
rachel: envoy config change could help, but need to test with our current model artifact servers. I'll spin up a perf test.
maria: good. closing thread for now, reopen if errors climb.
